questions.enonce_markdown:
Bring out clearly the place of the Holy Spirit in the Acts of the Apostles.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Acts of the Apostles is sometimes called the "Acts of the Holy Spirit", because the Spirit is the power behind the birth, growth and direction of the early Church. Luke presents the Spirit as the fulfilment of the promise of Jesus (Luke 24:49, Acts 1:8).

**1. The promise and the coming of the Spirit.** Before the ascension Jesus tells the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for the gift of the Father, and says that they will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon them and will be his witnesses "in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth" (Acts 1:4-8). At Pentecost the Spirit comes with the sound of a mighty wind and tongues like fire, and the disciples speak in other languages (Acts 2:1-13). Peter explains that this fulfils the prophecy of Joel about the outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh (2:16-21).

**2. The Spirit empowers witness and preaching.** After Pentecost, Peter, who had denied Jesus, preaches boldly and about three thousand are baptised (2:41). The believers are filled with the Spirit and speak the word of God with boldness (4:31), even before the council.

**3. The Spirit builds the community.** The Spirit is received through repentance and baptism (2:38). He is associated with fellowship, sharing of goods, joy and unity in the early church (2:42-47, 4:32-37). The lie of Ananias and Sapphira is called a lie to the Holy Spirit (5:1-11), which shows the Spirit's holiness and the seriousness of life in the community.

**4. The Spirit guides the mission.** Philip is told by the Spirit to approach the Ethiopian official (8:29). The Spirit tells the church at Antioch to set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work (13:2-4). Paul's party is hindered by the Spirit from preaching in Asia and from entering Bithynia, and is led to Macedonia (16:6-10).

**5. The Spirit opens the Church to the Gentiles.** At the house of Cornelius, while Peter is speaking, the Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile hearers, who speak in tongues, and Peter concludes that they should be baptised (10:44-48). When the church at Jerusalem questions this, the event is recognised as God's work (11:15-18). At the Council of Jerusalem the decision is introduced with "it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us" (15:28).

**6. The Spirit chooses and equips leaders.** The seven appointed to serve are to be men "full of the Spirit and of wisdom" (6:3), and Stephen is "full of the Holy Spirit" at his martyrdom (7:55). Barnabas is described as "full of the Holy Spirit and of faith" (11:24). Elders are made overseers by the Holy Spirit (20:28).

**7. The Spirit in the experience of all believers.** The Spirit is given to the Samaritans through the laying on of hands of Peter and John (8:14-17) and to disciples at Ephesus (19:1-7). He is given to all who believe, without distinction.

**Conclusion.** In Acts the Holy Spirit is the empowering presence of God: he gives courage to witness, unity to the community, guidance to the missionaries, and opens the door for the Gentiles. Without the Spirit the mission described in Acts would be incomprehensible.
